title: A scalable sample-based quantum diagonalization solver for general Pauli-sum Hamiltonians
abstract: A scalable ground-state solver to be used in sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) is presented. The solver is built on JAX API, and is intended to be run on GPU platforms and possibly many-GPU high-performance computing facilities. It is capable of subspace diagonalization in up to $2^{30}$-dimensional subspace, with possible upgrades to enable even larger-scale operations. The two main components, a general-purpose eigensolver and an SQD-specific matrix-vector operation function, are described in detail. Efficiency of the eigensolver with respect to the GPU memory is demonstrated using a simple physics model. Furthermore, good strong scaling of the eigensolver in many-GPU environment is observed.

bite.hook: A new GPU solver can diagonalize quantum subspaces up to 2³⁰ dimensions for sample-based quantum algorithms.
tldr: Created an open-source, scalable ground-state eigensolver for sample-based quantum diagonalization.
Implemented the solver using the JAX framework to run efficiently across single- and multi-GPU platforms.
Demonstrated GPU memory efficiency on a model system and verified strong scaling across multiple GPUs.
bite.whyItMatters: Hybrid classical-quantum algorithms rely heavily on classical supercomputers to post-process quantum samples. Pushing subspace diagonalization past a billion states expands the size of complex molecules and materials researchers can accurately simulate.
bite.eli5: Quantum computers generate huge lists of possibilities, but regular computers still have to do the heavy math to find the lowest-energy state. This new program uses graphics cards to solve those massive equations at an enormous scale.
